name: Amasa
overview: Amasa was a male member of the tribe of Ephraim known as the son of Hadlai. He is noted for aiding the defeated Judaites, demonstrating a role of assistance and possibly reconciliation between tribal groups. Beyond this, Scripture provides limited additional personal details about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Amasa means '[my] people are from Jesse,' reflecting a Hebrew origin. This proper name was not given directly by God, and no additional titles or names are recorded for him.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Amasa was the son of Hadlai, establishing a clear paternal relationship. No other family connections are documented beyond this in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Amasa's significance lies in his action of aiding the defeated Judaites, which highlights a moment of support and possibly unity within the divided nation of Israel. His involvement is specifically noted in 2 Chronicles 28:12, situating him within the historical context of intertribal relations during a time of conflict. This contribution, though brief, underscores the biblical theme of mercy and assistance among God's people.
